messages:
Sam Lee: Quick sync — BlueHarbor wants a short POC to validate 2k sustained QPS on our text-gen endpoint and sub-120ms p95 at 512 tokens. Can we run a smoke then a 30m soak?
Ira Chen: Sounds doable. Need to confirm model variant and region. Are they ok with gpt-small-quantized in us-west-2?
Devon Patel: They requested AES-HSM keywrap in their questionnaire. That won't change perf but will affect onboarding time (KMS setup).
Sam Lee: @Ira yes model = rwd-gpt-small-q8. Region: us-west-2 primary, failover to us-east-1 only if we need extra capacity.
Ira Chen: OK. Proposed runbook: 1) 5m smoke 200 qps ramp, 2) 30m steady at 2k QPS with 1% poisson jitter, 3) 10m step-down. Capture token-level latency and model fallback events.
Sophia Gomez: I'll wire up trace hooks so per-request model routing is annotated in logs. Need a sample load generator command from you.
Devon Patel: For cost quote: they'll want projected token spend for the 30m run + estimate for production 24/7 at 2k QPS. I'll need example prompt length distribution.
Sam Lee: Prompt distro: 60% short (40 tokens), 30% medium (150 tokens), 10% long (400 tokens). Response avg 120 tokens.
Ira Chen: Load command (wrk2 + simple python harness). Paste below:
```bash
wrk -t8 -c500 -d00:30 -s ./scripts/rwd_payload.lua --latency http://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
```
Lua payload picks prompt length per distro and sets header X-Model: rwd-gpt-small-q8
```python
# quick harness to vary tokens
import random, requests
for i in range(1000000):
  l = random.choices([40,150,400],[0.6,0.3,0.1])[0]
  payload = {"prompt":"x"*l, "max_tokens":120}
  requests.post(url, json=payload, headers={"Authorization":"Bearer $TOKEN"})
```

Sam Lee: Nice. Ops question — will continuous batching be enabled? That changes tail latency.
Ira Chen: Yes continuous batching on that pool, batch-size cap 64, batch-timeout 6ms. We'll record both aggregated and per-batch sizes.
Devon Patel: For pricing, give two numbers: hosted POC estimate (one-off for the run + short term burst) and monthly commit for dedicated 2k QPS. I'll circulate a draft invoice.
Sophia Gomez: Results capture: include p50/p95/p99 token latency, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, KV cache hit rate, and number of fallback model invocations.
ops-bot: @channel Deploy plan scheduled: canary pool ready at 1768675360, full pool at 1768675385. CI job: perf-smoke-blueharbor started. :rocket:
Sam Lee: Great. Can we also simulate network variance (50ms added) to see multi-region failover behavior?
Ira Chen: I'll add a netem rule on one client for 5m during the steady phase.
Devon Patel: BlueHarbor legal asked about data-at-rest SLA during POC — need to confirm ephemeral logs TTL and whether we can enable redaction. Sam, can you confirm?
Sam Lee: We can set logs TTL to 7 days and enable PII redaction for the helm job for this customer. Ops needs to approve.
Sophia Gomez: I'll take ownership of the result writeup. Template will include run parameters, raw CSVs, summary charts, and a short exec summary for sales.
Devon Patel: Sales asks if we can cap the run to avoid going over their free credits — add a soft throttle at 2.2k QPS and stop if token spend > $X.
Sam Lee: Agreed — set budget stop and notify sales channel.
Ira Chen: Running smoke now — initial 200 qps pass looks clean: p95 98ms, GPU util 42%. Starting ramp to 2k.
ops-bot: perf-smoke-blueharbor: step-up 500 -> 1000 -> 1500 -> 2000 qps completed at 1768675405.
Sophia Gomez: Early results (30s sample): p50 35ms, p95 112ms, p99 260ms, tokens/sec 58k, KV hit 71%. Collecting full 30m now.
Devon Patel: Looks decent. Once you have the CSVs I'll prototype the pricing breakdown for steady-state and burst.
Sam Lee: Thanks all — next updates after 30m soak. :thumbsup:
